title: Move a terminal to its next batch, in any space

blocks.text: Terminals settle at the end of the day, and from then on their transactions belong to a new batch. The switch keeps each terminal's profile, with its current batch number, in the Space under `profile.<terminal>`. In the tests the space is `tspace:`; in production it is `je:terminals`, so that the profiles survive a restart.
Finish `nextBatch` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/BatchNumbers.java`. When you're done, it returns the new batch number, and afterwards:

items: `profile(terminal)` shows that number, in a transient space and in a persistent one;
the terminal still has one profile in the space;
two sessions settling the same terminal at the same moment get two different numbers.

blocks.text: About five lines. One test uses a space that behaves like `je:`.

cases.says: each settlement returns the next batch number and keeps the rest of the profile
a persistent space hands back a copy, so the changed profile has to be written back
a current value is replaced, not appended, so the key keeps one entry
the read and the write happen under the space's lock, so two settlements at once get two numbers

origin.section: 12.5 A Transient Space Hands Back the Stored Object, and a Persistent One a Copy

concepts: A transient space hands back the stored object and a persistent one a copy, so a change is made to a clone and written back.
